how: A flag starter supplies coordinates and a miniature flag starter receives a helper before giving stripe instructions.
Calls recruit help for the main flag and for extending Polish pictures without establishing that all readers join.
A miniature flag proposal receives a bare acceptance before instructions follow.
Routing builders to an official chat does not establish a host moderation rule, a response to flooding or containment of canvas posts.
Builders debate national symbols, design scale and flag rules rather than agreeing on a picture once at the start.
A border maintenance report and a claim that the flag was saved keep the work visible in the thread.
Coordinates and stripe dimensions turn a flag proposal into instructions another builder can follow.
The evidence supports offering and welcoming a bot, but leaves successful operation, multiplied placements and effectiveness unobserved.
Maintaining borders, rallying defence and removing a swastika are specific tasks of keeping the placed work.
Neighbours settle a three-pixel border, invoke treaties and contest a claimed breach while the agreement remains a reference point.
Participants urge restraint, repair neighbours and apologise after learning that apparently empty space was reserved.
Mutual protection is promised conditionally, repair is reported as compensation and another room's request for numbers is refused.
An existing alliance is invoked to protect a neighbour while other coalition offers remain proposals rather than demonstrated commitments.
Speakers call for converting flags and replacing another group's writing, with collective authorisation unestablished.
A restraint objection receives a dismissive taunt and an appeal to preserve art receives a contrary advertising claim.
The prospect that a shield would spread builders thin makes available effort relevant to design scale.
Loss prompts a new target and a different object, but continued defence prevents treating these proposals as one completed collective relocation.
The declaration that the flag was saved marks a shared success during the event rather than completion of every intended design.
Participants recount loss and their own night of fighting without supplying a settled final history.
A friendship proposal during placement and later image labels do not establish a decision to preserve the collective or carry work elsewhere.
Naming the site event as April Fools does not establish a local prank takeover or a shared licence to treat its organising calls as jokes.
The local evidence combines official coordination and reported consensus without demonstrating a formal vote, elected leadership or the global prevalence claimed across rooms.
Partition rhetoric names no rival and historical rejection of a coalition does not demonstrate an inherited tie naming the target in an attack call.
Delayed agreement news and attribution to random attackers do not establish a dispute over who may bind the room.
Post-closure image labels do not establish cleanup of a preserved canvas or a contest over which historical version to keep.
Takeover proposals name neighbours but do not establish that these disputes existed before the canvas.
Origin stories and partition language mobilise work while national history is also invoked to reject a proposed collective.
A respondent disowns attacks as random while reporting personal repairs, distinguishing attributed placers from the organised plan.
A request to retain team numbers inside the flag receives a refusal, making the flag a host territory rather than only a neighbouring border.
A visitor opens a negotiation between rooms and answers the proposed boundary with a commitment to work something out.
Starting and calling for helpers can be the same public turn, leaving no separate starter-to-call temporal transition to establish.
The small build links a proposal, acceptance and instructions, but those turns alone do not verify that the call caused completed pixel placement.
The miniature flag proposal receives the bare acceptance that the tentative call-and-answer mechanism predicts.
Calls and routing instructions do not show that a canvas flood caused the host to regulate discussion.
The quoted plan title does not expose a template or its adoption, preventing a test of whether design talk was settled by a shared template.
Reporting the existing border and maintaining it occur in the same passage, so building and upkeep need not appear as successive public phases.
A bot offer after defence does not establish that timer-limited upkeep caused automation or that the offered bot was operated.
Defence and border disputes overlap, and an agreement-based alarm can renew defence rather than demonstrating an initial defence-to-negotiation causal transition.
A reclaiming call is answered by invoking the agreement to go under the neighbour, directly showing treaty-based restraint talk.
Shared defence appeals and reported help do not establish that shortage of hands generated the help or that a particular call caused it.
A border request elicits a conditional promise of reciprocal protection, while repair is explicitly offered as compensation for stray encroachment.
An appeal to stop the void together does not establish formation of a new coalition because of shared defensive pressure.
Later explicit takeover calls establish attack proposals, whereas the opening construction coordinates alone identify no rival or encroachment.
An expansion call over a neighbour receives a reasoned instruction to stop because an alliance already exists.
An attack proposal is met directly by invocation of an existing alliance rather than a new negotiation.
Proposed replacement of another group's writing becomes an exchange of objection and dismissive contest talk.
A loss-and-move proposal does not attribute defeat to insufficient hands, while the later concern about spreading effort thin concerns another design.
Reporting rescue and celebrating it coincide in one statement, supporting their connection without proving a separate report-to-celebration causal sequence.
Celebration and earlier loss reports do not identify a subsequent record-making act caused by marking success.
Neither the friendship invitation nor post-closure labels show a record leading to a decision to continue the temporary effort.
A deal's slow dissemination and renewed attacks do not establish that members challenged anyone's right to commit the group.
Builders are directed to another room or chat to learn the current plan before shared instructions can coordinate their output.
Agreements reached in another venue must have their news carried to placers, and that transmission can lag behind the settlement.
Agreement-based restraint depends on receiving the settlement and choosing to comply, even when a local consensus has been reported.
National history can make a proposed coalition unacceptable, so an invitation framed as kinship can receive historically reasoned refusal.

statement: Riffing together on a canvas detail
how: Participants turn an impossible performance counter into a joke and punchline, a local practice beyond identifying neighbouring pictures or organising pixel work.
